findings.reason: the section's central claim is that a section-enumerating walk cannot survive its gate, so the author must either converge these two doccheck walks on the new reader or add them to the named-exemption set and correct the done-when; as written the gate passes by the rule's blindness, which is exactly the "under-count at every review" failure §17 states it exists to eliminate, and the two duplicate `find_all("h2", id=True)` walks remain.
findings.text: §17 declares that the heading-walk rule, run at the head, reports "nothing in ... reckon/doccheck.py", but `_section_level_refs` (doccheck.py:984) and `_section_contract_findings` (doccheck.py:1053) each call `soup.find_all("h2", id=True)` — a soup locator whose first argument is a literal heading tag, which the rule as specified explicitly matches ("every call to a soup locator, find_all, find, select, select_one ... whose argument names a heading tag ... a literal h1 to h6"); §17 gives neither site a convergence instruction nor a named exemption, and each holds the document text (unlike the `_in_landed_section` exception §17 does name because it holds none)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the core proposal is one deep raw-text parser (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser`) behind two public projections (`structured_section_spans`, `plan_headings`) plus a machinery-marker predicate, with `_section_digests` and the coverage join module-private in `plan_review.py` and one small classification predicate in `reckon/_schema.py`; substantial behaviour (spans, identity, card recognition, prose slicing) is hidden behind few names rather than spread across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §17's section-enumeration consolidation leaves two heading walks in `reckon/doccheck.py` unconverged and unnamed, and its own done-when asserts the instrument reports nothing there.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16, §17 and §18 each name what they retire or move (`plan_fingerprint`'s public `legacy` flag retired; `landed_section_ids` and `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` moved rather than added) or state why nothing can shrink (each retained public reader keeps callers), so the four net public definitions are accounted for in each section's own text and no section adds surface silently.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections cite and reuse the machinery that already exists (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, `_TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions`, `roadmap.implementable_sections`, `list_plan_reviews`), and three of its censuses reproduce exactly on the checked-out tree (6 lines for `== "implementable"`, 14 `data-reckon` lines across 5 files, `section-landed` outside docstrings, `landed_section_ids` owned by `reckon/_store.py` and imported by `plan_review.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the additions that could read as thin layers state why the underlying machinery cannot simply be exposed: `strip_tags` (§16) is a function over the existing `_TAG_RE` kept public only because the consumer crosses the package boundary, with `count_open_decisions` re-expressed over it so the expression keeps one caller; `plan_headings` (§17) carries identity/level/text/span/card records rather than forwarding `structured_section_spans`.
